# An exploration of the Lorenz Attractor and Makie Animation

The lorenz attractor is a beautiful example of chaotic systems.
These are traditionally defined as systems that are deterministic but very small differences
in initial conditions lead to vastly different, seemingly unpredictable, outcomes.
They are defined by the following differential equations:

\begin{align}
\frac{dx}{dt} &= \sigma (y - x) \\
\frac{dy}{dt} &= x (\rho - z) - y \\
\frac{dz}{dt} &= x y - \beta z
\end{align}


::: {#4 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.julia .cell-code}
Base.@kwdef mutable struct Lorenz
    dt::Float64 = 0.01
    σ::Float64 = 10
    ρ::Float64 = 28
    β::Float64 = 8/3
    x::Float64 = 1
    y::Float64 = 1
    z::Float64 = 1
end
```

::: {#6 .cell execution_count=1}
``` {.julia .cell-code}
function step!(l::Lorenz)
    dx = l.σ * (l.y - l.x)
    dy = l.x * (l.ρ- l.z) - l.y
    dz = l.x * l.y - l.β * l.z
    l.x += l.dt * dx
    l.y += l.dt * dy
    l.z += l.dt * dz
    Point3f(l.x, l.y, l.z)
end
```

``` {.julia .cell-code}
function plot_lorenz(; fname="lorenz.mp4", hist_length=200, N_frames=1000, colormap=:viridis)
    attractor = Lorenz()
    points = Observable(CircularBuffer{Point3f}(hist_length))
    colors = Observable(Int[])

    fig = Figure()
    ax = Axis3(
        fig[1,1],
        protrusions=(0, 0, 0, 0),
        viewmode=:fit,
        limits=(-30, 30, -30, 30, 0, 50)
    )
    l = lines!(ax, points, color=colors, colormap=colormap, transparency=true)

    record(fig, fname, 1:N_frames, framerate=30) do frame
        push!(points[], step!(attractor))
        push!(colors[], min(length(points[]), 100))
        l.colorrange = (0, min(length(points[]), 100))
        colors[] = colors[]
        points[] = points[]
    end
end
```

## Interactive GLMakie Plot

The following code can be used to make the lorenz plot interactive.
It adds a run button which pauses/plays the simulation.
It also includes a menu to change the colormap used to show the history of the simulation.

::: {#14 .cell execution_count=0}
``` {.julia .cell-code}
menu = Menu(fig, options=["viridis", "inferno", "magma", "plasma"])

on(menu.selection) do cmap 
    l.colormap = cmap
end
notify(menu.selection)

run = Button(fig[2, 1]; label="run", tellwidth=false)
isrunning = Observable(false)
on(run.clicks) do clicks; isrunning[] = !isrunning[]; end
on(run.clicks) do clicks
    @async while isrunning[]
        isopen(fig.scene) || break
        push!(points[], step!(attractor))
        push!(colors[], min(length(points[]), 100))
        l.colorrange = (0, min(length(points[]), 100))
        colors[] = colors[]
        points[] = points[]
        sleep(0.001)
    end
end
```
